title: Inside BitGo Singapore’s Growth Story With Angela Ang
summary: We sat down with Angela Ang, Managing Director of APAC and President of BitGo Singapore, to talk about what's driving BitGo Singapore's growth, and where it goes next.
body_markdown:
## Key Takeaways:


-


**APAC client base has tripled since BitGo Singapore received its Major Payment Institution licence two years ago** , and BitGo Prime trading volumes in Singapore more than doubled in the first half of 2026 versus the same period last year.


-


**Institutional demand in the region has shifted from "if" to "how"** . Clients are now asking how digital assets fit an existing operating model, not whether to adopt them, and that shift holds independent of price cycles.


-


**Custody, trading, financing, and settlement operating as one stack** , rather than across separate providers and jurisdictions, is what lets institutions put custodied assets to work instead of just storing them.


*The BitGo Singapore team at the company's new office.*


Two years after[BitGo Singapore Pte. Ltd. (BitGo Singapore) received its Major Payment Institution licence](https://www.bitgo.com/resources/blog/bitgo-singapore-expands-bitgos-apac-presence/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=apac&utm_campaign=singaporeapacgrowth) from the Monetary Authority of Singapore, BitGo Singapore's regional client base has tripled and BitGo Prime's Singapore desk, now the largest trading desk in BitGo Prime globally, has more than doubled trading volumes in the first half of 2026. The growth coincides with the opening of BitGo's new Singapore office, the regional hub for a headcount that has also more than doubled over the same two years.


We sat down with **Angela Ang, Managing Director of APAC and President of BitGo Singapore** , to talk about what's driving that growth, and where it goes next.


## The evolution of BitGo Singapore


Ang joined BitGo Singapore after more than a decade at the Monetary Authority of Singapore, where she helped build the city-state's payments and digital asset licensing regime, followed by a stint leading APAC public policy at TRM Labs. That background shapes how she reads the moment.


"Clear, proportionate regulations give serious firms room to build," Ang said. "Regulatory clarity builds trust with customers and gives institutions certainty to make long-term investments. That conviction is what I worked on from the regulatory and policy side of the table, and it's the same conviction that made the operator's seat at BitGo Singapore a natural next step."


BitGo's global licensing footprint has been a strategic advantage with regulated institutional customers, Ang said, because it gives them a clear benchmark for the standards BitGo is held to, one reason growth has tracked institutional adoption rather than the other way around.


## From custody to infrastructure


BitGo Singapore's APAC client base has tripled since the MPI licence, and Ang points to BitGo Prime as the clearest expression of where that relationship goes next. "Clients who came to us to custody assets are now also asking how those assets can work harder for them," she said. "Trading against global liquidity. Financing against the same collateral. Settlement that doesn't require assets to leave custody to execute. Holding assets safely is the entry point; helping clients put them to work is where the relationship goes."


That shift is why institutions are finding[BitGo Prime](https://www.bitgo.com/products/prime/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=apac&utm_campaign=singaporeapacgrowth) 's model works better for them, Ang said, pointing to Singapore volumes more than doubling in the first half of 2026 against the same period last year.


Rather than assembling[custody](https://www.bitgo.com/products/qualified-custody/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=apac&utm_campaign=singaporeapacgrowth) , trading, and[settlement](https://www.bitgo.com/products/go-network-oes/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=apac&utm_campaign=singaporeapacgrowth) across separate providers and jurisdictions, where every leg adds a counterparty, a settlement window, and a reconciliation process, Ang described a model where the stack stays together. "The client trades across a network of exchanges, market makers, and liquidity providers, seeking the best available price, without the assets leaving qualified custody to execute.[Financing](https://www.bitgo.com/products/financing/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=apac&utm_campaign=singaporeapacgrowth) sits against the same collateral, in the same place. The stack stops being something the client has to stitch together."


"Custody was never the destination," she added. "It was something that had to exist before anything else could be built on top of it. The point lands harder in this region, because the fragmented alternative is more fragmented in Asia Pacific than anywhere else."


## Building locally, connecting globally


Singapore's advantage, Ang said, is that it's a global financial centre that's also a hub for digital asset innovation.[Assets under management in the city-state stand at SGD 6.7 trillion](https://www.mas.gov.sg/publications/singapore-asset-management-survey) , with roughly three-quarters sourced from outside the country, and Singapore is home to[more than 2,000 single-family offices](https://www.mas.gov.sg/news/parliamentary-replies/2026/written-reply-on-sfos) , the pool Ang expects the next phase of institutional adoption to come from: asset managers, family offices, private banks.


*Angela Ang, Managing Director of APAC and President of BitGo Singapore, speaking on a panel at BitGo's Singapore office opening, part of a discussion on 'Built in Singapore: Regulation, Trust, and the Institutional Digital Asset Playbook.*


"Regulatory clarity is what converts proximity into trust," Ang said. "Institutions in this region won't allocate to an asset class without being able to explain their counterparty to their board and their regulator." Singapore's digital asset regulatory regime, in place since 2020, answered that question earlier than most jurisdictions, one reason many of the region's early institutional movers are based there.


The commercial position has followed: BitGo Singapore has more than doubled its Singapore headcount in two years, and the city now hosts BitGo Prime's largest trading desk.


Asked what success looks like two years from now, Ang framed it as a continuation of the build phase already underway. "We're only just entering the institutional era of digital assets in earnest," she said. "Regulated institutions across the region are setting up their foundations now, and much of what we do today is that work, setting up the operational and compliance plumbing that has to be built before anything runs at scale. Two years out, success is having converted that foundation into volumes that move the region's market structure."

## Frequently Asked Questions


### Is BitGo Singapore a separate licence from BitGo's other regional entities?


Yes. BitGo Singapore Pte. Ltd. operates under its own Major Payment Institution licence from the Monetary Authority of Singapore, alongside BitGo's other regulated entities globally.


### Does using BitGo Prime to trade mean assets leave qualified custody?


No. BitGo Prime lets clients trade without assets leaving qualified custody to execute.


### Which institutions is BitGo Singapore built for?


Regulated financial institutions, payment service providers, fintechs, digital asset businesses, family offices, and accredited and institutional investors across the region.


### Is Singapore's regulatory regime new?


No. Singapore has had a regulatory regime for digital assets in place since 2020, and BitGo Singapore has held its MPI licence since August 2024.
